title.en: Evaluate a postfix expression with a stack

say.en: Give a stack the postfix expression 7 8 2 star 4 / plus and it finds the answer in one left-to-right pass, with no brackets and no precedence rules. In this lesson: Evaluate a postfix expression with a stack.
Keep the operand order right for minus and /.
Detect an invalid expression.

body.en: Read the *expression* from left to right. Push every operand onto the stack. When an operator comes, pop the top element as B and the next as A, compute A operator B, and push the result. At the end, if exactly one element remains on the stack, it is the value of the expression; otherwise the expression is invalid.

points.en: Operator → B = pop, A = pop, push A op B
End: one element = result; otherwise invalid

say.en: Operator gives B equals pop, A equals pop, push A op B.
End: one element equals result; otherwise invalid.
Read left to right. Operands are pushed: 7, then 8, then 2.
Star pops 2 as B and 8 as A, computes 8 times 2 equals 16, and pushes 16.
Push 4. Then slash pops 4 and 16 and pushes 16 divided by 4, which is 4.
Plus pops 4 and 7 and pushes 11. One value remains: the answer is 11.
Order matters for minus and divide: the first value popped is the right operand B.
